conviction_note: Six small findings net to -0.7. On this stock the guide has set the sign of every recent print (beat plus reaffirm went +7.6 and +15.2, beat plus cut went -4.4 and -13.9). The macro and aluminum negatives agree with a 23% slide since 30 June that had already absorbed Tecnoglass's 6 August print, and the EPS bar is unresolved, so I emit -0.4, about 0.3 below the sum.
bar: Revenue: company guide on the Q1 FY27 call (26 Jun 2026) of Q2 net sales 'slightly lower' YoY against $358.2M (Q2 FY26, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/6845/000000684525000154/a83025fy26q2results.htm), against a single wire consensus of $359.46M (https://www.tradingkey.com/markets/stocks/apog/forecast), so consensus sits slightly above the company's own guide. Adjusted EPS: UNRESOLVED. MarketBeat has $0.81 from 2 estimates ranging $0.50-$1.11 (https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NASDAQ/APOG/earnings/), while TradingKey/TradingView show $0.63. The company guided only 'lower YoY' against $0.98. My own segment arithmetic gives about $0.72-0.80. Every EPS-linked finding is capped small. FY27 guide is $2.70-3.25 adj EPS against street ~$2.82-2.88.
positioning_check: Short interest 935,284 shares, 4.5-4.6% of float, 4.2 days to cover, settlement 2026-09-15, up 11.3% from the prior period (https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NASDAQ/APOG/short-interest/ ; https://equibles.com/stocks/apog/short-interest). Building but not crowded. Options: chain unusable (no two-sided ATM quotes, zero open interest), so there is no skew and no implied move; the baseline falls back to the 12.72% median historical reaction. Tape: -5.9% over 20d, -27.7% from 52w high; insider Form 4 prices show $45.74 on 2026-06-30 against $35.37 spot. No open-market insider buying or selling since June; only grants and one gift (https://stockcircle.com/insider-trades/apog).

findings.finding: Tecnoglass's Q2 release (6 Aug 2026) says the all-in US aluminum price rose about 77% YoY. Its gross margin fell 740bp to 37.3% and it trimmed full-year guidance on 'sustained elevated aluminum costs'. Apogee's Q2 FY26 Architectural Metals comp is its toughest of the year (14.8% adj EBITDA margin on $140.9M). Against that, LME fell from a $3,855 peak on 2 Jun to about $3,239 by 21 Aug, so Apogee's spring-set surcharges may have widened the spread late in the quarter. Net: a small negative for Metals margin.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Metals margin and input-cost commentary drove the Q1 FY27 beat (+15.16% on 2026-06-26, Metals margin 7.3% to 11.2% on surcharges). The cost headwinds that drove the Q2 FY26 guide cut were followed by -4.44% (2025-10-09).
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. Apogee peaked near $43.5 on 7 Aug, the day after the Tecnoglass print, and fell about 19% since, which is what pricing a cost read-through looks like. What is left is the exact Metals margin against the 14.8% comp, which only two analysts model. The LME decline during the quarter cuts the other way and is equally visible, so the net is small.
findings.independence: LME/Midwest premium path (https://aegis-hedging.com/insights/metals/daily-first-look/2026-08-21 ; https://discoveryalert.com/aluminium-prices-iran-war-smelter-disruption-2026/). Apogee itself on 26 Jun called input costs 'very volatile' and said surcharges would offset them (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/06/26/apogee-apog-q1-2027-earnings-call-transcript/). Net of the rest: Services (backlog $734.5M, +8%) should grow, and Glass faces an easier margin comp in Q2 (16.1%) than in Q1 (18.3%).

findings.finding: GroGlass closed on 18 Sep 2026, after Q2 ended: about $30M first-year revenue at about 25% adj EBITDA margin, funded from cash and the revolver. Kalwall closed 1 Jul (about $85M/yr at 15%). The company said it would give GroGlass financials on the Q2 call, so the FY27 net-sales guide ($1.43-1.48B incl. Kalwall) should rise mechanically by roughly $12-15M. EPS accretion in FY27 is near zero after interest and amortization.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guide direction has set the sign of the last four prints: reaffirm or new guide gave +7.59 (2026-04-24) and +15.16 (2026-06-26); cuts gave -13.89 (2026-01-07) and -4.44 (2025-10-09).
findings.why_not_priced: The deal terms are public, but no estimate has a GroGlass-inclusive revenue guide: the one revenue consensus ($359.46M Q2) and the FY street numbers predate any company quantification. If it were priced, FY revenue estimates would already sit above the $1.43-1.48B range. Financing question answered: the revolver draw buys a 25%-margin coatings business, not distress (leverage 1.3x, $419M revolver availability per the Q1 10-Q).
findings.independence: Completion release https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000006845/000000684526000093/exhibit991-pressrelease.htm. It is the same company, so not truly independent. Q1 10-Q liquidity: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000006845/000000684526000063/apog-20260530.htm

findings.finding: The company guided Q2 net sales 'slightly lower' YoY against $358.2M, a figure that includes about two months of Kalwall (roughly $14M), while the one revenue consensus is $359.46M. The wire's revenue number therefore sits slightly above the company's own guide, so a small headline revenue miss is the base case.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Revenue has rarely led this stock; the guide and EPS have. Q1 FY27 revenue fell 1.1% YoY and the stock rose 15% on the EPS beat and the reaffirm.
findings.why_not_priced: The guide is public, so this lands inside what the company told the market to expect. The only unpriced part is that the aggregator's number did not follow it. With two analysts that gap can persist, and the headline will read as a miss.
findings.independence: Consensus figure: https://www.tradingkey.com/markets/stocks/apog/forecast. Shares the transcript with finding 6.

findings.finding: Fortify Phase 2 cut SG&A from 19.7% to 16.4% of sales in Q1 FY27, and the street under-modelled it: adj EPS was $0.57 against $0.43. The savings ($13-15M annualized) carry into Q2. My segment arithmetic puts Q2 adj EPS at about $0.72-0.80, a beat against the $0.63 aggregator figure and roughly in line with MarketBeat's $0.81. The bar is unresolved, so this is capped small.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: EPS beats: +$0.14 in Q1 FY27 (stock +15.16) and +$0.14 in Q2 FY26 (stock -4.44, because the guide was cut). Beats pay only when the guide holds.
findings.why_not_priced: With two estimates as far apart as $0.50 and $1.11, a 'beat' headline is likely on at least the feeds carrying $0.63. If the savings were fully modelled, the two sources would converge near $0.75-0.80.
findings.independence: Estimate spread: https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NASDAQ/APOG/earnings/ and https://www.tradingkey.com/markets/stocks/apog/forecast. The arithmetic shares the Q1 release with finding 1.

findings.finding: Short interest rose 11.3% to 935k shares (4.5% of float, 4.2 days to cover) at the 15 Sep settlement, while the stock fell from $45.74 (30 Jun) to $35.37 into a print where the company has reaffirmed its range twice in a row.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: A reaffirm off a depressed base went +15.16 on 2026-06-26. No squeeze history on record at this SI level.
findings.why_not_priced: Building shorts plus a 23% drawdown means a reaffirm would meet sellers who are already out, and some covering. At 4.5% of float this is not a crowded short, so the mechanism is small.
findings.independence: Equibles same FINRA data (https://equibles.com/stocks/apog/short-interest) - same underlying source, not independent.

findings.finding: Management's H2-weighted FY27 guide rests on 'anticipated improvement in underlying market conditions'. Nothing published since it spoke shows that improvement. The ABI was 46.6 in July and 47.2 in August, still contracting, with firms expecting declines rising from 21% to 29%. The Dodge Momentum Index fell 0.4% in August, and commercial planning excluding data centers is down 18.9% YoY. That raises the odds of narrowing the range toward the low half.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guide cuts gave -13.89 (2026-01-07) and -4.44 (2025-10-09), the second despite a $0.14 EPS beat.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the stock is down 23% since June and the FY street (~$2.82-2.88) already sits below the $2.975 midpoint, so a narrowing to about $2.70-3.00 would be roughly in line. The unpriced part is a cut below $2.70, or no narrowing at all. This is a macro-to-company proxy; the company has confirmed only that Glass is hurt by soft new construction.
findings.independence: Dodge Momentum Index Aug 2026 (https://www.construction.com/dodge-momentum-index-flat-in-august/), a different series pointing the same way. The H2-improvement quote comes from the Q1 transcript shared with finding 3.

baseline_tension: No skew or implied move exists. The two macro/aluminum negatives agree with the -5.9% 20d run-up and the -27.7% distance from the high, so they are probably mostly priced; the small positives (GroGlass in the sales guide, Fortify-driven beat against a low aggregator bar) cut against the run-up.
lessons_applied: Rule 5 (unconfirmed macro proxy is small): ABI/Dodge guidance finding cut from -1.5 to -1.0. Kept, not dropped, because the company itself tied the H2 guide to improving conditions.
Rule 5 (an unexplained drawdown is worth 0): positioning finding cut from +0.4 to +0.2, keeping only the sourced rise in short interest and not the bounce-from-drawdown inference.
Rule 6 (the finding lands inside the company guide): revenue-vs-consensus finding cut from -0.4 to -0.3, since the company already told the market Q2 sales would be slightly lower.
Rule 6 (bar unresolved, $0.63 vs $0.81): Fortify/EPS-beat finding capped from +0.6 to +0.5, and the bar field says the EPS bar is unresolved.
Rule 1 / Rule 3 (reaction follows the guide; the caveats agree with the run-up): emitted move -0.4, below the -0.7 sum (pre-lessons draft -0.6).

Left standing: aluminum finding (-0.6, already netted against the LME decline under the read-the-set rule) and GroGlass guidance finding (+0.5; financing question answered as an acquisition, not distress).
